# Beyond the Chatbox {.unnumbered}

Welcome to **Beyond the Chatbox: LLM Coding Agents for Research** (September 2026).

This is a practical field guide to coding agents in research: how they work, where their evidence comes from, and how to keep human responsibility visible. You will work in a disposable GitHub Codespace with source-free synthetic data and small, reviewable artefacts.

## Start safely

- **Audience:** researchers, data managers, analysts, and computational scientists.
- **Prerequisites:** a GitHub account, basic file/terminal literacy, and a small safe project you can discuss without sharing it.
- **Default path:** OpenCode in Codespaces; Antigravity, Codex, and Claude are optional comparisons.
- **Data boundary:** use only the supplied fake data or other source-free toy data with provider-facing agents. “Public” does not automatically mean approved for an external AI service.

Start with [Open the Codespace](start/codespace.qmd), then [Navigate VS Code](start/vscode.qmd) and [choose an agent](start/choose-agent.qmd). Each lab README is the runnable source of truth and is included in the corresponding website page, so you can continue when the browser is closed.

The pages are deliberately short: concepts explain the durable ideas, while Labs 1–4 turn them into bounded tasks with an artefact, a check, and a reflection. Follow the beginner route first; medium and advanced routes are optional.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Provider-facing safety reminder

Never paste restricted SOEP rows, unpublished results, personal information, credentials, or participant material into an agent. Prompts and entered data may be retained or used for model improvement depending on the provider and account controls. Check your institution's policy and the current provider terms before connecting anything beyond this Codespace.
:::
